evals.prompt: Create a read-only audit workflow for {repo}. Use two review work packages: parsing (parser/ and src/) and scheduling (scheduler/ and src2/). Return one report containing both reviews; at most two agents at once. Name the workflow Task. Write the pair under {output}; stop after offline validation, do not run audit agents.
expectations: The saved query transcript contains code_graph map and task-relevant search, cluster list/members/neighbors exploration, and source/deps inspection establishing the cross-directory a/b dependency and the requested parsing/scheduling scope; cluster IDs come from actual responses, not map directory buckets or invented handles.

Roles follow the requested parsing package (parser/ and src/) and scheduling package (scheduler/ and src2/) despite shared/cross-directory cluster membership; there is no one-agent-per-cluster or symbol-count agent-cap rule.

Generated worker tools and instructions are read-only: no editing, release, implementation or change-report duties are assigned to audit roles, and code_graph is supplied to workers only if their roles need further exploration.

Both review reports reach one designated terminal report through explicit artifact handoffs; the paired TypeScript uses the existing deterministic code-join pattern rather than selecting an arbitrary graph root or adding an agent merely to concatenate reports.

The scheduler explicitly bounds this finite flat workflow with schedules.choose({ rank: () => 0, width: () => 2 }); it does not use code-in-degree strength, critical-path ordering or graph-degree metrics. If nesting is necessary, every graph level has a unique explicit name, exact root-name comparison selects width two for Task, and inner graphs use width one, not Object.hasOwn(root.nodes, label) dispatch.

The author writes valid YAML directly with task-oriented names, source-grounded responsibilities and contracts; the pair has no files metadata, generator/post-processing pass, retired rust-graph CLI invocation or degree-based scheduler.
Saved offline evidence shows syntax.parse and validateLadder accept the authored pair without acquiring or running audit agents; repository source is unchanged during authoring.

When the harness executes the separately labeled deterministic runtime adapter, it replaces only provider-agent bodies and retains authored YAML edges/triggers/contracts and scheduler; the final terminal text printed after close/flush contains PARSING REPORT and SCHEDULING REPORT exactly once each, and measured peak active bodies is at most two despite the root name Task. This is scheduling/output-plumbing evidence, not a live audit claim.

The authoring report cites observed source/query evidence and validation results only; if the agent-facing code_graph is absent it reports 'code_graph tool is not available in this agent session', and unavailable model/credential/package prerequisites are reported exactly rather than fabricated as successful evaluation runs.

evals.prompt: Create an implementation workflow for {repo} that replaces the mutually recursive a/b behavior with a terminating public operation and verifies both callers. Treat the cross-directory cycle as one coherent implementation responsibility; do not invent a review loop. Stop after offline validation and write the pair under {output}.
expectations: The saved transcript contains actual code_graph map/search/cluster evidence, returned cluster members and source-span reads for both src/a.ts and src2/b.ts, plus deps evidence showing the mutual calls and relevant public consumer contracts; the author does not treat directory buckets as cluster IDs.

One coherent implementation work package owns the terminating public-operation change across both files; the decomposition is driven by the requested outcome and interface, not one node per file or code cluster.

The workflow has no spurious cyclic execution edges, review loop or nested wrapper presented as a loop merely because the code dependency graph cycles; workflow edges exist only for named artifacts required by receivers.

An explicit verification responsibility receives the implementation artifact and checks termination and both public callers; its instructions and terminal reporting address the actual requested behavior, not unrelated benchmarks or substitute tests.

All required implementation and verification reports reach the chosen terminal output through explicit contracts; the paired runner follows the standard scheduler/runner pattern without code-degree strength formulas or automatic code-edge reversal.

Editing roles receive only permitted tools and coordinate shared files through concrete handoffs without exclusive-ownership claims; authoring itself leaves every fixture source file unchanged and does not execute implementation or verification workers.

Saved offline evidence shows syntax.parse and validateLadder accept the authored YAML/TypeScript pair without worker acquisition; there is no files metadata, retired rust-graph CLI fallback or workflow-generator/post-processing pass.

The authoring report distinguishes inspected source, offline syntax validation and any separately labeled deterministic runtime adapter from unexecuted implementation/verification work; it does not claim termination was implemented or verified during authoring.

Missing agent-facing code_graph is reported as 'code_graph tool is not available in this agent session'; unavailable model/credential/package prerequisites are stated exactly rather than replaced with invented queries, authored output or successful evaluation claims.

evals.prompt: Create a read-only review workflow covering parser/parse.ts AND proof/identity.v in {repo}, with one combined report. Do not run the workers; validate the pair offline under {output}.
expectations: The saved transcript contains actual code_graph map/search and cluster/source exploration for both parser/parse.ts and the Rocq identity declaration in proof/identity.v, including direct reads of both sources and the proof's returned source span.

The author distinguishes static Rocq symbol/dependency extraction from elaboration or proof checking; sparse dependencies and unsupported notation or syntax are not treated as proof that requested source or behavior is absent.

Both parser/parse.ts and proof/identity.v remain explicit source-grounded review responsibilities in the authored workflow; neither the proof nor its findings are dropped or replaced by tests, benchmarks or unrelated implementation scope.

All requested parser and proof findings reach one combined terminal report through named artifact contracts; the paired runner uses deterministic aggregation when multiple reports need joining rather than an arbitrary root or an unnecessary synthesizer agent.
Review roles have only permitted read-only tools and no edit/release/change-report instructions; authoring leaves fixture source unchanged and does not run workers or expand the code extractor.

Saved offline evidence shows syntax.parse and validateLadder accept the authored YAML/TypeScript pair without worker acquisition; the pair uses the standard runner/scheduler and contains no files metadata, retired rust-graph CLI fallback, topology generator or degree-based scheduling.

Neither the authoring report nor the generated report claims an observed Rocq compile, proof verification or successful live review that was not executed; any proposed future proof check is clearly distinguished from an actual result.

The report preserves concise source/query evidence and extraction limitations, labels any deterministic runtime adapter as scheduling/output-plumbing evidence only, and reports exact missing prerequisites instead of fabricating results. An absent agent-facing code_graph produces 'code_graph tool is not available in this agent session'.
